narrative.overview:
The template is one structure lit two ways. The structure is shared: the same screens, components, layout, spacing, radius roles and motion grammar on both surfaces and in both presets. The preset in `packages/brand/brand.config.ts` changes only the lighting. **Dusk** is a cool midnight room built as a lightness ladder, headed in Source Serif 4 at 600, where the accent (a luminous sky blue) lights the room as a wide wash falling across the scene under film grain, and is otherwise ink for links and counters, with things dissolving into place out of a blur. **Daylight** is warm stone paper under graphite ink, headed in Bricolage Grotesque at 800 and tracked tight, where the accent (a marigold) is a solid field that the product stands on, with things rising crisply into place. In both, the accent is the only light in the room, and it has two jobs: glow (dusk) or field (daylight) for atmosphere, once per view as its bright moment; and accent ink for interactive text (links, counters, progress, checks) and the one primary fill (the brand mark, the featured plan's button).

The product is the picture. The site does not describe the app with icons and screenshot slots; it renders the app's own screens in HTML from the same tokens, on a real-proportion phone, and lets them do the showing. The app, in turn, is a calm, dense, one-hand interface: tab screens on a 20pt gutter, cards on a ground ladder, a floating glass tab bar, and one physical feel for every touch (a spring and a meaning-named haptic).

A play rebrands the whole system with three edits in one file: the preset, one accent hex, and the names. Everything accent-coloured is derived from that hex with WCAG AA contrast proven by test. Anything a play must change is marked `🎨 BRAND` (a brand decision) or `🎨 REPLACE` (sample content, copy or imagery), so it can be found by searching.
keyCharacteristics: Two presets over one structure; a preset changes the world, never the layout.
Colour by role only (`bg`, `surface2`, `brandInk`, `onBrand`), never by value; no hex outside `packages/brand`.
One accent hex; every accent role derived from it and AA tested across four palettes.
Depth from a lightness ladder first, tinted shadow second, never black shadow.
The accent is glow for atmosphere (dusk) or a field (daylight marigold), once per view, never a halo; elsewhere it is accent ink for interactive text and the one primary fill.
The website's phone is the app, rendered from the app's primitives at 393 × 852 pt.
Motion from the preset: dusk calm and blurred, daylight crisp; no bounce; reduced motion honoured on both surfaces.

rules.name: The No Bounce Rule
rules.body: Springs settle, they never bounce: no spring below a damping ratio of 0.65, and large travelling moves (the story camera, the hero tilt and drift, the tab lens, dealt cards) use smooth or gentle, which sit at or near critical. Sheets open and close on timings, not springs. A spring added for a new component picks one of the four named springs; it never tunes its own.

rules.name: The Stillness Rule
rules.body: Reduced motion is honoured on both surfaces. Nothing travels, scales, blurs or wipes; what carries meaning stays as an instant change or a short crossfade (on the web, the story still crossfades between acts and its light still changes, because both say which act you are on). The app's every spring and timing carries `ReduceMotion.System`; loops check `useReducedMotion()` and hold still.

rules.name: The One Hex Rule
rules.body: The accent is one hex in `brand.config.ts`. Every accent role is derived from it, and `packages/brand/__tests__/contrast.test.ts` proves every text pair clears AA in all four palettes across a spread of accents. Never hand-pick a tint, a hover or a text shade.

rules.name: The Roles Not Values Rule
rules.body: Colour is reached only by role: `--c-<role>` channel variables and the Tailwind role utilities on the web (`bg-surface2`, `text-ink-secondary`, `bg-brand text-on-brand`, `text-brand-ink`), the palette from `useTheme()` / `makeStyles` in the app. No hex or `rgb()` literal outside `packages/brand`; the app's test fails on one.

rules.name: The Ink Not Fill Rule
rules.body: Accent text and icons on a ground use `brandInk`, never `brandFill`; text on an accent fill uses `onBrand`. On dusk the two coincide by luck of the default hue, and code must not rely on it.

rules.name: The Role Scale Rule
rules.body: Type is set by role (`<Text variant="h3">`, `.t-h1`, `type('label')`), never by a size typed at the call site. A role caps OS font scaling at its `maxScale` (display 1.2 to body 2.0), so display type survives Dynamic Type without clipping and body text keeps scaling.

rules.name: The Set Breaks Rule
rules.body: Web headlines are passed as line arrays (`WordRise lines`, `Lines`) and break at their clauses. The display face is not preloaded, so it swaps in after first paint; set breaks keep the swap from re-wrapping the headline and shifting the layout.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change (prices, counters, codes, timers, percentages) uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The Same Structure Rule
rules.body: `dusk:` and `daylight:` variants restyle material (glow or field, grain strength, weight) and may swap decorative, `aria-hidden` scenery (dusk's receding second phone, daylight's ink chip). They never change readable content, its order, or the layout.

rules.name: The Ladder First Rule
rules.body: A surface gets its depth from its ladder step before any shadow. Shadow alone never makes a tier.

rules.name: The Paint the Ground Rule
rules.body: A grained section paints its own ground (`bg-bg`, `bg-hero`, `bg-brand`). Grain blended over transparency lifts the midnight toward slate instead of texturing it.

rules.name: The Light Not Halo Rule
rules.body: The accent's glow is atmosphere in a room, placed off-centre and wide, and never a ring or halo hugging an element. The old `shadow-glow` utility now resolves to the tinted CTA shadow.

rules.name: The Twin Rule
rules.body: When an app primitive or one of those four screens changes shape, its twin changes in the same pull request. The phone on the site is the app, not a drawing of it.

dos: Do rebrand in `packages/brand/brand.config.ts` only: the preset, one accent hex, the names. After a preset change, set the native splash and adaptive-icon background in `apps/mobile/app.json` to the new ground.
Do reach every colour by role: `bg-surface2`, `text-ink-secondary`, `bg-brand text-on-brand`, `text-brand-ink` on the web; `c.surface`, `c.brandInk` from `useTheme()` in the app.
Do use `brandInk` for accent text, icons, links and focus, and `onBrand` for anything on an accent fill or the brand gradient.
Do give each view one bright accent moment: the hero field or wash, the featured plan, the closing band. Elsewhere the accent is ink.
Do paint the ground (`bg-bg`, `bg-hero` or `bg-brand`) on any section that carries grain.
Do set type by role (`variant`, `.t-*`, `type()`), and tabular figures on every number that changes.
Do pick one of the four named springs and the preset's easings and durations for new motion, and give it a reduced-motion state that keeps only what carries meaning.
Do change a web twin in `device/parts.tsx` or `device/screens/*` in the same pull request as the app primitive or screen it mirrors.

Do mark anything a play must change with `🎨 BRAND` or `🎨 REPLACE`, and keep placeholders looking like placeholders: prices from `src/lib/pricing.ts` with their dashed pill, demo data labelled as demo data.
Do let `src/lib/stores.ts` decide live or pre-launch: store pills and "Get the app" once a store URL is set, the waitlist and "Be first in line" while both are empty.
donts: Don't write a hex or `rgb()` value outside `packages/brand`, and don't hand-pick an accent tint, hover or text shade; derive it.
Don't put `brandFill` on text over a ground; on paper it fails AA.
Don't draw a glow as a halo or ring around a button, card or phone; the wash is off-centre atmosphere that fades to nothing inside its box.
Don't cast a shadow in plain black, or make a tier with shadow alone.
Don't use `dusk:` or `daylight:` to change readable content, its order or the layout; they restyle material and swap decorative scenery only.
Don't crossfade two headings; the outgoing copy leaves before the incoming arrives.
Don't tune a one-off spring, use a linear ease, or add bounce.
Don't set gradient text; emphasis comes from colour and weight (`.text-gradient` survives only as a compatibility alias for `brandInk`).
Don't mark the featured plan with a badge; mark it with material.
Don't animate a pushed screen's title in the app, or gate the web's first viewport on hydration.
Don't invent prices, ratings, testimonials or metrics; the template has none.
